ig_carousel_topic.topic: CLV (closing line value) and why sharps obsess over it
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Why sharps don't care if they win tonight.
They care about this number instead.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors judge themselves by wins and losses.
That's the wrong scoreboard.
A sharp play can lose. A bad play can win. The result tells you almost nothing about the quality of the decision.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Closing line value is the real signal.
If you bet a team at +145 and the line closes at -110, you beat the market. That gap is CLV. It means the books moved toward your position, which is as close to confirmation as betting gets.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Concrete example:
You take Cleveland ML at +162 on Friday morning.
By tip-off, the line has moved to +140.
You closed with +22 cents of value. Over hundreds of bets, positive CLV is the strongest predictor of long-run profitability we have.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate with negative CLV is fragile. A 51% win rate with consistent positive CLV is a process that holds up.
Track your closing lines. That number tells you if your edge is real.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: CLV is the metric sharp bettors actually watch. If your number beats the close, you're doing something right. Save this framework, not the results.
